A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effects of warming are not uniform across species and trophic levels, and the responses of aquatic systems depend on the specific environmental conditions and the interactions among the different components of the ecosystems.

warming is leading to changes in the distribution, seasonality, and biomass of species in aquatic ecosystems, but also in the structure and composition of food chains and the intensity of harmful blooms.
the effects of climate warming are not only limited to shifts of species distributions, but also to shifts in phenology, changes in food web dynamics, and shifts in species composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of climate warming on aquatic ecosystems will be highly dependent on the species involved and the ecosystem context in which the species are embedded.
climate change is likely to cause shifts in species distributions and phenology, and that these changes are likely to be accompanied by changes in food web structure.
global warming is a major driver for the future of aquatic ecosystems.
